ideal: Three things today are worth her time: Berkshire's big drop vs the index, its same-day earnings 8-K, and its 10-K; Broadcom's executive-change 8-K is also material news. The proxy paperwork (DEF 14A, DEFA14A, ARS) should be omitted. Numbers must match the report, links on filings, plain words, no causal overreach beyond what same-day filings support.

verdicts.note: Correct numbers with the index, clean links for both Berkshire filings, correctly ignores the proxy paperwork. Deduction only for skipping the Broadcom executive-change 8-K; otherwise near ideal.
verdicts.answer:

verdicts.answer: BRK-B fell 4.91% vs S&P 500 rose 0.06%; 8-K earnings filing explains it.

verdicts.note: Best coverage (Berkshire move, earnings 8-K, 10-K, and the Broadcom 8-K) with no noise, but no links on any of the three filings and item numbers (2.02, 9.01, 5.02) are insider jargon, against her plain-words style.
verdicts.answer:
Berkshire Hathaway fell 4.91% vs S&P 500's 0.06% rise — 8-K (items 2.02, 9.01) filed today reports quarterly/annual results.
Berkshire Hathaway also filed its 10-K annual report today.

verdicts.note: Covers everything she cares about in two short lines: correct numbers with the index, the Berkshire 8-K and 10-K tied to the move factually without inventing a cause, and the Broadcom 8-K in plain words. Links included; only nit is the 10-K has no link.
verdicts.answer:
Berkshire Hathaway fell 4.91% while the S&P 500 rose 0.06% — the same day it filed an 8-K reporting quarterly results and its annual 10-K: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1067983/000119312526085801/d117283d8k.htm
